seoTitle: Free Regex Test Case Runner: Should Match, Should Not Match
metaDescription: Run one regex against lists of strings that must match and must not match. Get pass or fail for each line. Free and local.
intro: Checks one JavaScript regex against many test strings. Mark each line as must match or must not match and see which ones pass.
why:
A regex that works on the three examples you tried can still accept bad input or reject good input. A list of positive and negative cases catches both kinds of mistake and gives you a small regression test to keep with the pattern.

Put "+ " before a string that should match and "- " before one that should not. The tool runs them all and prints PASS or FAIL per line with a count. You can match anywhere in the string or require the whole string to match, which is what most validation patterns need.
howTo: Enter the regex in the first box.
Write test cases in the second box, one per line, starting with "+ " or "- ".
Choose anywhere or whole string matching.
Fix the pattern until every line shows PASS.

faq.q: Why do lines need a + or - prefix?
faq.a: The prefix says what you expect. Lines without a prefix are ignored, so you can leave comments or blank lines in the list.

faq.q: What is the difference between the match modes?
faq.a: Anywhere means the pattern may match a part of the string. Whole string wraps the pattern in ^(?:...)$ so all of it must match.

faq.q: Does it support other regex engines?
faq.a: No. It runs the JavaScript engine. Behaviour can differ in PCRE, Python and Java.

faq.q: Can a pattern hang the page?
faq.a: A pattern with catastrophic backtracking can. Run it through the ReDoS checker first if you are unsure.
